why: EQUIVALENT, not a coverage gap, and measured rather than assumed: the trim's skip for a piece whose solid wall would cut the floor cannot fire under `runs`' placement rules. `fits()` keeps every piece cell's 3x3 neighbourhood clear of any other wall and of the piece's own rotated image, and no piece sits on the outer ring, so every wall component is one isolated straight or L bar with open floor all round it, and a lone bar cannot enclose floor. An instrumented copy turned 3542 pieces solid over seeds 1-1000 in each of nine configurations (default, minRun=4, confine=off, both, run=6-12 with and without the confinement, pieces=10, pieces=24, lane=5cell; 9000 boards) and the skip fired 0 times; with it removed all 9000 boards were byte-identical. Kept so that a piece shape that can touch another wall is what flips this to killed, rather than a trim that silently walls off floor.
